title: Hedging and Stance in Academic Writing
text:
Scientists often use hedging language when they describe findings that are not yet fully confirmed. Phrases such as 'it appears that' or 'the data tentatively suggest' signal that a claim is provisional rather than definitive. Such cautious wording protects researchers from overstating their results. It also invites readers to evaluate the evidence for themselves.

Stance, by contrast, refers to the writer's overall attitude toward a claim. A writer who states that a theory 'is certainly correct' takes a strong position, whereas one who writes 'is possibly correct' adopts a more tentative one. Readers, therefore, rely on these markers to judge how much confidence the author actually has.

questions.text: According to the passage, what do phrases such as 'it appears that' signal?
options: That a claim is provisional rather than definitive
That a claim has been proven beyond doubt
That a report is too long to read
That the research sources are listed

questions.text: What does the passage say the term 'stance' refers to?
options: The number of references in a paper
The writer's overall attitude toward a claim
The length of a research article
The date a study was published

questions.text: What can be inferred about researchers who use cautious wording?
options: They want to avoid overstating their results
They have no evidence to support their work
They prefer to write very short texts
They do not expect readers to check their claims

questions.text: Why would a careful reader pay attention to markers such as 'possibly correct'?
options: They confirm that the theory is wrong
They replace the need for any evidence
They help the reader judge how confident the author is
They make the sentence grammatically shorter

vocabulary.definition: describing something as bigger or more certain than it really is
uncertain and not yet fully decided
careful to avoid risk or mistakes

paragraph_translations: Учені часто використовують пом'якшувальні формулювання, коли описують результати, які ще не повністю підтверджені. Фрази на кшталт «здається, що» або «дані обережно вказують на» сигналізують, що твердження є попереднім, а не остаточним. Таке обережне формулювання захищає дослідників від перебільшення своїх результатів. Воно також спонукає читачів самостійно оцінити докази.

Натомість позиція стосується загального ставлення автора до твердження. Автор, який стверджує, що теорія «безперечно правильна», займає сильну позицію, тоді як той, хто пише «можливо, правильна», обирає більш невпевнену. Тому читачі покладаються на ці маркери, щоб оцінити, наскільки впевнений автор насправді.
